items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: I was not a great specimen of Charles Atlas type

ctx.x: But however, naturally, we were more or less predominantly in black neighborhoods, but they were always nice neighborhoods and of course my father and mother being cultured people, our home was as clean and nice as the next person's, you know. But it was this time that I became aware of my athletic ability because there were times I had to protect myself as a boy. You know, when you carry a violin under your arm, and you're not too big -- you know, I was not a great specimen of Charles Atlas type, you know, and…

But many times when I'd come down the street with my violin, many of the boys would challenge me, you know, I mean want to take my violin away from me. Well, now everything they would say to me would be, I could take. They'd call me names or whatever or not, but when they grabbed that violin boy, they were in trouble.
